writtenTo: Lovers and all who celebrate marital love
importantNotes: The Song affirms that romantic love and physical intimacy in marriage are good gifts from God.
Jewish tradition read it as an allegory of God's love for Israel; Christians see Christ and the Church.
The repeated refrain 'Do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires' teaches sexual purity.
'Love is as strong as death' (8:6) — one of the most powerful statements about love in Scripture.
Solomon wrote 1,005 songs (1 Kings 4:32); this is his greatest — the 'Song of Songs.'

chapters.1: The bride longs for the beloved; she describes her own beauty and his affection.
chapters.2: The beloved is like a lily among thorns; the season of love has come; do not awaken love prematurely.
chapters.3: The bride searches for her beloved in the night; Solomon's wedding procession arrives.
chapters.4: The bridegroom praises the beauty of his bride from head to toe — she is flawless.
chapters.5: The bride delays and the beloved withdraws; she describes his beauty to the daughters of Jerusalem.
chapters.6: The beloved is found; he praises her unique beauty among all women.
chapters.7: The bridegroom delights in the bride's beauty; they plan to enjoy the countryside together.
chapters.8: The power of love — 'Love is as strong as death'; a final celebration of committed love.
